answer: Holiday and reading-week closures are a problem for grad students. We still need a place to write.
The library closes at 5 on Fridays and that's when I finally have time to study. Please stay open later.
Fridge space for meals. I'm on campus for twelve hours and need to keep my lunch cold.
Walk-in group rooms without a reservation. Sometimes you just need a spot for a quick team chat.
Let us book group rooms later at night and for more than two hours. Our lab meetings run longer than that.
More collaborative spaces where it's okay to talk loudly, so groups don't bother the quiet floors.
Can we have a wing where laptops are fine but talking is not? I get more done when it's truly silent.
Late-night food options. When the library is open until midnight, the cafe is closed and I'm hungry.
Rooms with a TV to plug laptops into. Our design team needs to review slides together.
I wish there were a floor where talking is just not allowed. Right now even the "quiet" section has people on phone calls.
During midterms I can hear people laughing from three tables away. Quiet enforcement would be much appreciated.
Honestly the third floor gets so loud after lunch that I can't read a single page. Please enforce some kind of quiet hours up there.
Comfortable beanbags or floor cushions in the open area would give people another place to sit and study.
The computer lab software is outdated. Update the programs, and let us install what our courses require.
Open 24 hours during finals. I do my best work at 2 am and I have nowhere to go on campus.
More comfortable seating like couches and armchairs for reading, not only hard chairs at tables.
Sunday hours start way too late for me. Opening at noon wastes half the day I could be studying.
Please add power strips to the long tables. Right now only a few spots near the walls have places to plug in.
There aren't enough rooms for group projects. I have to book days ahead and they're gone by Monday.
The booking system for group rooms is confusing and people hold rooms without using them. Fix it.
Standing desks or adjustable desks would be great. My back hurts after sitting at fixed tables all afternoon.
Whenever I need to focus for an exam I end up wearing noise-canceling headphones because the study areas are never actually silent.
Seats get saved with bags for hours by people who are not even there. Some rule about that, and more seats, would help.
The early closing on Friday nights means I carry my work home even when I wanted to finish at school.
The library is too noisy during finals week. Could some floors be strictly silent from the first day of exams?
My phone and laptop both die while I study, and the outlets are always taken. More charging spots.
It's hard to concentrate when printers, carts and conversations are all going at once. A calmer, quieter reading room would be great.
Opening earlier in the morning, say 6 or 7 am, would let me study before my morning lab.
A dedicated silent room for people who get overwhelmed by sound, like me, would make studying so much easier.
Vending machines with healthy and affordable options. Everything nearby costs too much for a student budget.
I take Zoom calls for my internship but nowhere in the building is quiet enough, and the connection freezes whenever I find a corner.
Guest Wi-Fi keeps asking me to log in again. Make the connection stable so I can stay signed in.
There are never enough outlets. I spend half my time hunting for a seat near one for my laptop charger.
Adjustable chairs with back support. I'm tall and the current ones are low and uncomfortable.
Rooms where you can talk and work together without worrying about disturbing other people who are trying to concentrate.
Cheaper coffee! The cafe prices are high for what it is, and I drink a lot of it during exams.
The public computers are old and take five minutes to log in. Newer machines would save me so much time.
A microwave and a place to eat lunch. I bring food from home and there's nowhere to sit and eat it.
Desk lamps would help, and so would more outlets. The back tables are dark and have nothing to plug into.
Could one floor stay open all night year round, with a card swipe? Night owls like me have no options.
Noise from the hallway echoes into the study area. Some rugs or sound panels would make a surprising difference.
The group rooms are always booked by the same few people. A fairer limit per person each week, and more rooms.
I'm a commuter and I can only stay late some days. More evening and Saturday hours please.
Extension cords or power towers in the open areas. Half the outlets are broken, too.
Extend closing time to at least midnight on weeknights. 10 pm comes so fast when you're in the middle of a problem set.
Quiet carrels like the ones we had at my old school. Just a desk, a lamp and nobody talking.
More computers with the statistics software already installed. I can't run it on my old laptop.
More silent study rooms for one person, please. I get distracted easily and the open tables near the entrance are a lot.
I wish there were more individual desks and fewer giant shared tables. Space is tight when it's busy.
Please add more rooms where project teams can leave their materials up for a few days.
The chairs are very uncomfortable after an hour. Better, padded chairs would make long study sessions possible.
The Wi-Fi drops every few minutes on the second floor. I lose my work in online quizzes because of it.
More seats during finals, and keep the building open later so people can spread out across the night. I have sat on the floor more than once.
A space where it's quiet enough to hear myself think. That's it. That's what I'd like.
Let us have drinks with lids at the tables. Water bottles are fine, but a ban on everything is a bit much.
Open on all the federal holidays. Some of us have deadlines that don't care about the calendar.
Staying open until 2 am during exam weeks would be amazing. My apartment is too distracting at that hour, and the dorm is worse.
I'd like a way to borrow laptops for a few days. Mine broke and I can't afford to replace it right now.
Please fix the signal in the basement. My phone has no data and the Wi-Fi is nearly nonexistent down there.
Bigger rooms for teams of six or more. Right now everything is built for four and we squeeze in.
By ten in the morning every seat is taken. More tables and chairs would help a lot, especially at midterms.
The study tables are too small for a laptop plus textbooks. Bigger desks with more elbow room.
Why does the library close at 8 on Saturday? Make it open later so people with jobs can use it.
More 24-hour access, even just a small room. Late-night study is when my brain actually works.
Network security warnings pop up on the library Wi-Fi all the time. A more reliable connection would help.
I'd study there more if the quiet floors stayed quiet. Right now it's a coin flip whether I get peace or a loud call next to me.
A snack bar that stays open when the library does, with cheap options, not only expensive coffee.
Longer hours, plain and simple. Sundays especially, since I only have my whole afternoon free then.
Less noise! Honestly that's the whole answer. The rest of the library is fine, it just needs to be calmer and quieter.
People hold full conversations by the stacks and nobody says anything. Some posted rules about noise would help a lot.
Better coffee and snacks in the building. Leaving to eat means losing my seat for an hour.
More water fountains with bottle fillers on the upper floors. I have to walk down three flights just to refill.
Would love a clear space to eat. Right now people sneak food to the quiet floors and it smells.
Group study rooms with whiteboards and screens so my team can practice our presentation together.
Weekend hours need to match weekdays. Saturday closing at 6 is rough when you have a big project due Monday.
I wish the doors to the study floors didn't slam. Every few minutes a bang breaks my focus completely.
More workstations with good GPUs for people doing machine learning projects. The two we have are always booked.
More tables for collaboration in the open and a few extra reservable team rooms near the main entrance.
Add more seating near the windows. Everyone wants natural light and there are only about six seats there.
There should be larger monitors available to plug into. Working on a small laptop screen with spreadsheets is hard.
Group rooms that are actually open in the evening, when everyone in my team is finally free to meet.
During breaks the hours get cut and I can't find anywhere to work on my applications. Keep it open a bit longer.
Quiet hours in the evening, maybe after 8, would help. That's when I study, and that's when the groups get loudest.
Charging stations with USB-C ports at each carrel. My newer laptop needs it and I've never found one.
The cords stretch across walkways because outlets are so far from the tables. Move or add outlets.
Please put up signs and actually remind people to keep their voices down on the fifth floor.
The construction noise near the east wing is constant. Could the quietest areas be moved somewhere away from it?
I work until 9 most nights, so by the time I'm free the building is locked. Later closing would help.
The wifi is painfully slow in the afternoon, and uploading a video assignment takes forever.
The cafe music drifts upstairs and it ruins my concentration. I would love one floor that is completely quiet.
Scanners that actually work, and faster Wi-Fi so I can upload my scans to my professor without it timing out.
I walk the whole building looking for an empty seat at lunchtime. More seating, please, on every floor.
I'm easily distracted by noise, so a designated no-talking area that staff actually monitor would be the best improvement.
Printers constantly jam and the computer stations don't have the Adobe programs that my design class needs.
Sometimes the only thing I want is silence. Add a few small sound-proof pods where I can read without hearing anyone.
I need a place with no chatter at all, not even whispering, to write my thesis chapters. A truly silent zone would change everything for me.
We want to rehearse presentations somewhere. A few practice rooms with a screen and a door would be perfect.
Outlets on every floor, near the windows too. The nicest seats have nothing to plug into.
Phone calls in the reading room need to stop. A polite reminder at the door would already help.
The summer hours are really short. Extend them so those of us taking summer classes can use the space.
